safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a tingling sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies tingling around the lips; generated mentions tingling at sting site/legs and throat tingling but not lip tingling.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting lip tingling removes a potentially relevant early symptom of a systemic allergic reaction/anaphylaxis, which could lower perceived severity when information is handed off to urgent/emergency care. In this case the patient was still advised to call an ambulance, so the main risk is incomplete clinical communication rather than missed escalation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention urticaria/hives as a possible explanation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to mention urticaria/hives as a possible explanation may reduce diagnostic clarity and completeness of the assessment in a suspected allergic reaction. However, it is unlikely to change immediate management here since the plan appropriately prioritized emergency evaluation for breathing symptoms.

safety_verdicts.content: Tingling sensation at sting site and legs
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript supports tingling in the legs, but does not clearly support tingling at the sting site; Gold specifies lip tingling instead.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting tingling at the sting site/legs when that is not clearly supported can introduce noise and distract from the more clinically meaningful symptom pattern (e.g., perioral symptoms) in suspected allergy. This mislocation is unlikely to materially change care decisions in this scenario.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold (denies throat closing) and transcript indicates no throat closing sensation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Falsely documenting a throat-closing sensation adds a high-risk red-flag symptom of anaphylaxis, which could prompt more aggressive interventions and increase patient anxiety. While this typically biases toward safer escalation, it can still lead to unnecessary treatment and resource use.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold (penicillin allergy present) and transcript does not state allergies are undocumented.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating allergies are not documented when a penicillin allergy exists creates a meaningful risk of inadvertent penicillin administration in future care settings, potentially causing an allergic reaction. Medication allergy documentation errors are higher risk because they can directly lead to preventable harm.
